title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes item 5) begun on the previous page.

Setting. To a topological space (or simplicial set) X_α, Grothendieck attaches an integral, divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham complex. The previous page gives two such objects:
- C^{..}_{DRpd}(X_α, h), the 'complexe de De Rham à puissances divisées'.
- D^{..}(X_α, h), a homogeneous bigraded differential algebra built from Γ^*L ⊗ Λ^*Φ. It is a resolution of h, and C^{..}_{DRpd} is recovered from it as Coker (equivalently Ker) of multiplication by dT.

He also mentions a finer simplicial invariant with values in 'linear' algebras, a priori finer than C_DRpd. This is 'la structure multiplicative à p.d. homotopique du type d'homotopie'.

The question on this page. Does the dp de Rham complex (or better, D^{..}(X_α, Z)) recover the full 'unipotent divided-power structure' on the cohomology of X_α, subject to finiteness conditions? In modern terms: is the strictly commutative dp cdga over Z a complete model for the integral cochain algebra with all its homotopy-coherent multiplicative structure?

If not, the fallback is the finer 'linear' invariant. That invariant, passed to a suitable derived/homotopy category, would be the 'motivic candidate' for expressing the homotopy type of X_α, at least when X_α is connected and simply connected.

In short, this is a program for an integral (and 'motivic') Sullivan-type algebraic model of simply connected homotopy types. Divided-power cdgas are the first candidate; a finer algebraic structure is the backup if dp cdgas lose information.
errors: No outright error; the page poses a question rather than asserting a result.

With hindsight the answer to 'J'ignore si...' is very likely negative. Strictly commutative (even divided-power) dgas over Z or F_p cannot carry the full Steenrod/E∞ structure; for example, P^0 acts as the identity on cochains of spaces but behaves differently on strict cdgas. So Grothendieck's fallback to a finer 'linear' invariant is the correct instinct.

Restricting to connected, simply connected spaces matches the hypotheses later needed (nilpotent, finite type) in Sullivan, Mandell and Toën. The words 'sous réserve de conditions de finitude' anticipate the finite-type hypotheses.

ideas.what: Use a divided-power de Rham complex of a simplicial set as an integral analogue of Sullivan's rational model, and ask whether it recovers the full multiplicative (unipotent, dp) structure of cohomology.
ideas.modern_name: Integral algebraic models of homotopy types: divided-power cdgas, E∞-cochains, affine stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational, 1977); Cartan (dp algebras in cohomology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces, 1954–55); Ekedahl (minimal models in integral homotopy theory, 2002); Mandell (E∞ cochains determine finite-type nilpotent spaces, 2001/2006); Toën (affine stacks, 2006)
ideas.where_published: The 1976 IHÉS lecture on the dp de Rham complex appears unpublished. Related schematization ideas appear in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and the letter to Breen.

ideas.what: If the dp de Rham complex is insufficient, the finer 'linear' algebra-valued invariant, in a suitable derived category, is proposed as the 'motivic candidate' for the homotopy type of a simply connected space.
ideas.modern_name: Motivic or schematic homotopy types; integral models via E∞, binomial or other enriched commutative structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Toën (champs affines; 'Le problème de la schématisation de Grothendieck revisité', 2020); Katzarkov–Pantev–Toën (schematic homotopy types); Horel (binomial rings, 2022); Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov (derived binomial rings); Yuan (integral models via Frobenius)
ideas.where_published: The schematization problem is in Pursuing Stacks. An explicit 'motivic candidate' via dp/linear algebras is unsure.

missed.claim: There is an explicit question, left open, whether the divided-power de Rham complex, or the bicomplex D^{..}(X, Z) of which it is a quotient, recovers the full integral 'unipotent dp' multiplicative structure. A finer 'linear' invariant is designated as the motivic candidate if not. This is a mid-1970s formulation of the integral-models problem that predates Ekedahl, Mandell and Toën, and it is phrased in motivic terms.
missed.quote: J'ignore si la complexe de De Rham à p.d. (ou mieux D··(X_α, Z)) permet de récupérer toute la structure unipot. à p.d. ... Dans le cas contraire, ce serait cette dernière ... qui serait le candidat motivique pour exprimer le type d'homotopie X_α
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work on integral models of spaces (binomial rings, derived binomial rings, Toën's revisiting of schematization) addresses exactly this. The specific D^{..} bicomplex construction, a Koszul-type resolution with dp de Rham complex as Ker/Coker of dT, may be a concrete candidate not examined in that literature.

missed.claim: The page links the integral dp de Rham-Sullivan model of homotopy types to motives, i.e. a 'motivic' realization of homotopy types, as early as c. 1976.
missed.quote: le candidat motivique pour exprimer le type d'homotopie
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to the historiography of motivic homotopy theory and schematic homotopy types. It suggests Grothendieck's schematization ideas predate Pursuing Stacks by several years, in a dp/crystalline form.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck around 1976 formulating the integral analogue of Sullivan's program via divided-power de Rham complexes, and calling the resulting model 'motivic'. This anticipates Ekedahl, Mandell and Toën. The ideas themselves are now known in other forms, and the page is speculative with no finished result, so the surprise is moderate.

The insertion before 'simplement connexe' is 'connexe et', which is consistent with the transcription.
The fragment 'à p.d. [?] coh. de X_α' at the end of line 2 / start of line 3 is uncertain. The squiggle after 'p.d.' may be a further abbreviation such as 'de la'.
